name: npc-object-pool-cap
summary: Zone.exe pre-sizes the NPC object pool at 256 per process. A zone hosting many maps runs out and every further NPC is dropped with 'NPCManager::nm_SetNPC : Too many npc'. Raise the pool size.
status: DOES NOT WORK - DO NOT APPLY. Built and statically verified 2026-09-15 (npcs=2048), but the zone got WORSE: zone01 went from 35 'Too many npc' asserts and READY, to 545 asserts and never reaching IOCP WORKTHREAD #12 RUNNING in 8 minutes. Reverted. The pool's slot table is self-contained (ShineObjectPool::Create heap-allocates (count+1)*0xC and vtable+8 bounds-checks against [this+4]), so something ELSE is sized by the 256 - most likely the NPC HANDLE range, which is a u16 shared with mobs and players (nm_SetNPC does 'add eax, 0x21' / 'push 0x21' around the handle). Find what else consumes that 256 before trying again.

target.note: Chained builds need --allow-hash-mismatch; no other recipe touches this site.

npcs.why: ShineObjectPool::Create reads its count as a WORD ('mov ax, word ptr [ebp+8]', stored to [this+4]) and treats 0xFFFF as the 'no pool' sentinel, so 65534 is the last usable value. Cost is only memory: the pool allocates (count+1) * 0xC bytes for its slot table, so 2048 is 24 KB against the stock 3 KB.

why: NPCs are allocated from a typed object factory, not from a fixed array, so the assert is an ALLOCATION
FAILURE rather than a bounds check - there is no 'cmp' to relax:
NPCManager::nm_SetNPC
0x004C6645   push 4                      ; object type 4 = NPC
0x004C664A   push ecx                    ; &out handle
0x004C664B   mov  ecx, 0x132826B8        ; the object manager singleton
0x004C6650   call 0x0054FE20             ; factory Alloc
0x004C6659   cmp  edi, esi               ; NULL?
0x004C6663   push 0x006C5AD0             ; "NPCManager::nm_SetNPC : Too many npc"
the factory switches on the type id and each type has its own sub-pool:
0x0054FE8A   cmp  eax, 0xC / jmp [eax*4 + 0x550070]
case 4 ->  0x0054FEDF   lea ecx, [esi + 0xCC] ; call 0x004025D0   (pool Alloc)
the manager's constructor sizes every sub-pool in turn, and +0xCC is the NPC one:
0x00557622   push 0x5DC  ; lea ecx,[esi+0xAC]   (1500)
0x0055765C   push 0x100  ; lea ecx,[esi+0xCC]   (256)  <-- THIS ONE
0x00557696   push 0x3E8  ; lea ecx,[esi+0xEC]   (1000)
0x005576D0   push 0x1F40 ; lea ecx,[esi+0x10C]  (8000, the mob pool)
ShineObjectPool::Create (0x005546F0) then heap-allocates the slot table:
movzx eax, ax / inc eax / mov edx, 0xC / mul edx / push ecx / call 0x00654F0B
so nothing else is sized by the 256 and no relocation is needed - the single imm32 is the whole patch.
Zone-wide, not per map: every map's NPCs share the one pool, which is why splitting maps across zones
postpones the problem instead of fixing it.

edits.why: ShineObjectManager ctor: NPC sub-pool (+0xCC) element count
